points erased by penalties.counts: Scores taken off the board by the SCORING team's own accepted foul on the scoring play itself: the play-by-play says "TOUCHDOWN NULLIFIED", "FIELD GOAL IS GOOD, NULLIFIED" or "SAFETY NULLIFIED". Any foul type counts (holding, offensive pass interference, illegal formation, illegal use of hands...). TD = 6, FG = 3, safety = 2. The player charged is the one flagged on that play.
points erased by penalties.doesnt_count: Offsetting penalties (the down is replayed). A defensive foul on a made field goal (the kicking team chose the yards). Fouls earlier in the drive. Defensive fouls like DPI that HELPED a score (that's the other team's foul). Points the drive scored later anyway are not subtracted.
points erased by penalties.src: src/deep_stats.py (tp_ptsnull, pn_ptsnull); every play is listed in the rare_plays lookup (type wiped_score)

penalties.counts: Accepted penalties only (declined and offsetting don't count), by nflverse penalty type, charged to the flagged player and his team; also split by the unit (offense, defense, special teams).

success rate.counts: A play is a success if it gains 40%+ of the yards needed on 1st down, 60%+ on 2nd, or converts on 3rd/4th. Lost fumbles are failures.

run stop.counts: A defender credited with a tackle (solo or assisted) on a run that failed by the success-rate rule. Close to PFF's run stop.

stuff.counts: A run that gained 0 yards or lost yards. Defender stuffs: he made the tackle. RB stuffed %: his carries that gained 0 or less.

short yardage.counts: 3rd or 4th down with 2 or fewer yards to go; converted = a success by the success-rate rule.

3rd down (player).counts: QB 3rd-down conversion % and receiver 3rd-down numbers include 4th downs too (down 3 or later).

red zone.counts: Plays snapped at the opponent's 20 or closer. Goal line = the 5 or closer.

clutch.counts: QB dropbacks in the 4th quarter or overtime with the score within 8 points (one score).

deep / short throws.counts: Deep = 20+ air yards. Short (pass defense) = 5 air yards or less. Air yards = how far past the line of scrimmage the ball was thrown.

big plays.counts: Runs and catches of 10+, 20+ or 40+ yards, by yards gained on the play.

EPA.counts: Expected points added (nflverse model): how much a play changed the expected points of the drive, based on down, distance and field position. Per dropback = his passes, sacks and scrambles.

CPOE.counts: Completion % over expected (nflverse): actual completions minus the expected rate for each throw (depth, distance, location). +5 = 5 points better than expected.

pressure / bad throws (QB).counts: Times pressured and bad throws are Pro Football Reference charting (via nflverse), so they can differ a bit from PFF or NGS.

blitz.counts: FTN charting (via nflverse): a dropback is a blitz when 5+ rushed or a linebacker or DB blitzed. Charting services define this differently, so a few % gap vs PFF is normal.

offensive line on-field numbers.counts: Pressure %, sack % and yards per run on plays the lineman was on the field for (nflverse participation, 2022+). They are his LINE's results with him out there, NOT pressures or sacks he allowed himself (no free source charts that).

defender pressures / hurries / coverage.counts: Pro Football Reference charting via nflverse (pressures, hurries, targets and yards allowed in coverage, missed tackles). Charting, so other services may count a few differently.

frauds / over-achievers.counts: Skill players vs ESPN's weekly projections in the games they played: weighted % below (frauds) or above (over-achievers) their projection.

injuries (% healthy).counts: Every team's health weighted by who is hurt (a starting QB counts about 10x a punter). Out/IR = all of his value, Doubtful 3/4, Questionable 1/4.

season pace.counts: His per-game average x a full regular season (17 NFL, 12 college). Assumes he plays every game left.

heisman race.counts: Production per game vs his position (QBs: pass + rush yards, 20 per TD, minus 45 per INT; others: rush + rec yards, 20 per TD), each game weighted by the opponent's strength, 100 = 10th best at his position; then times team success, popularity (Wikipedia views, 30 days) and position (QB x1.1, RB x0.85).

trade watch.counts: 0-100 score from the team's playoff chance (10,000 simulations), contract ending soon, age, role (snap share), value and trade headlines in the last 2 weeks. QBs and RBs count less. Best fits = contenders weak at his position. No cap-space data.

coach score.counts: 0-100 (50 = average head coach): 35% wins over expected, 30% record vs winning teams (short records pulled toward average), 15% postseason wins per season, 10% team lift (vs the year before he arrived), 10% cupcake padding (share of wins vs losing teams, and FCS teams in college; counts against him). Hot seat = this season vs expectations, the program's usual standard and recent seasons.

records (gold tags).counts: The NFL's official individual records (Wikipedia list), only flattering ones, refreshed weekly.

our rankings.counts: The site's # is the Default blend of the factor scores plus head-to-head results. See the model factors below for what each score means.

college.power: Opponent-adjusted scoring margin, capped so blowouts of bad teams don't count extra.
college.resume: Strength of record: how many more wins than an average top-25 team would have with this schedule.
college.efficiency: Opponent-adjusted EPA/play and success rate, garbage time removed.
college.sos: How hard was your road? The average strength of the FBS teams you played, no matter how good you are. FCS games are left out here (they count in Cupcake). Higher = tougher schedule.
college.recent: How the team has played in its last few games.
college.cupcake: How much did you pad it? Only the games far below YOUR level count: FCS opponents, plus below-average teams 14+ points worse than you (bigger mismatches count more). A bad team playing other bad teams isn't padding. Higher = more padded, and it counts against the team. Only games already played count.
college.luck: Higher = has had bad luck: lost games they statistically won, so the record undersells them. Lower = has been winning coin flips.

nfl.power: Team strength in points from our NFL model: opponent-adjusted scoring margin (capped at 17) blended with EPA per play, with last season carried over, recent weeks counting a bit more, and a small boost (or ding) for the head coach.
nfl.resume: Strength of record: how many more wins than a top-8 team would have with this schedule.
nfl.efficiency: Opponent-adjusted EPA per play (offense minus defense).
nfl.sos: How hard was your road? The average strength of every opponent played. Higher = tougher schedule.
nfl.recent: How the team has played in its last few games.
nfl.cupcake: How much did you pad it? NFL teams can't pick cupcakes, but schedules still hand them out. Only real mismatches count: the opponent has to be clearly bad (about the bottom quarter of the league) and 5+ points worse than YOU, with full credit at 10+ points worse. A bad team playing other bad teams isn't padding. Higher = more padded, and it counts against the team. Only games already played count.
nfl.luck: Higher = has had bad luck in close games (one-score results are treated as coin flips). Lower = has been winning coin flips.

injuries.name: Alec Ingold
